full_judgment:
Mr. Syed Md. Ziaul Karim, J:- This Rule calls in question the legality and propriety of judgment and decree dated 29.06.2000 passed by learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Barguna, dismissing Title Appeal no.40 of 1995 and affirming those of dated 25.05.1995 passed by learned Assistant Judge, Amtali, Barguna Sadar, decreeing Title Suit no.147 of 1992 

2. Short facts leading to this Rule are that on 01.12.1992, opposite party nos.1-2 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit no.147 of 1992 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Amtali, Barguna Sadar, impleading petitioner and opposite party nos.3-57 as defendants for setting aside ex-parte judgment and decree dated 28.10.1991 passed by learned Assistant Judge, Amtali Barguna Sadar, in Title Suit no.4 of 1988 instituted by Abdul Khaleq as plaintiff against Hatem Ali and others as defendants for partition in respect of 9.35 acres of land out of 21.17 acres described in Schedule of plaint. 

3. The plaintiffs case put in a nutshell are that they are owners in possession in their land at this stage defendant nos. 1-19 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit no. 04 of 1988 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Amtali, for partition impleading plaintiffs as defendant nos.11 and 14 respectively and others. Summons of suit were not duly served upon them but the same were fraudulently shown to have been served by the relations of plaintiffs of Title Suit no. 04 of 1988. The present plaintiffs i.e. defendant nos. 11 and 14 of Title Suit no.04 of 1988 did not receive any summons by post even they had no knowledge about the suit and ex-parte decree dated 28.10.1991. On 25.08.1992 for the first time they came to know about such ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit no.04 of 1988 Hence the suit. 

4. The defendant no.15 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all materials allegations made in plaint contending interlaid that plaintiffs had full knowledge about Title Suit no.04 of 1988 as they had no title in the suit land so they willfully did not contest the suit. Just only to harass the defendants plaintiff instituted the instant suit. Thus the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

5. On the pleadings defferent issues were settled including issue of maintainability and issue whether plaintiffs are entitled to get a decree as prayed for. 

6. In course of trial plaintiffs examined three witnesses, of them P.W.1, Begum (Plaintiff no.2) who proved their title and possession in suit land and also proved that summons of Title Suit no.04 of 1988 were not duly served upon them. P.W.2 Md. Matiar Rahman, P.W.3 Motahar Hossain were examined to corroborate the evidence of P.W. I . They proved their documents which were exhibited and marked as exhibits 1-9. The defendants examined three witnesses, of 
them D.W.1 Rashia (defendant no.15), D.W.2 M.A. Rahim, Process Surveyor and D.W.3 Hafijuddin Munshi, they proved that notices were properly served. 

7. After hearing learned assistant Judge by judgment and decree dated 25.05.1995 decreed the suit and set aside exported decree passed in Title Suit no.04 of 1988. Against which defendant no.15 as appellant preferred Title Appeal no.40 of 1995 in the Court of District Judge, Barguna, which was ultimately heard by learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Barguna who by judgment and decree dated 29.06.2000 dismissed the appeal and affirmed those of trial Court. 

8. Feeling aggrieved defendant no. 15 as petitioner preferred the instant application and obtained the present Rule. 

9. Mr. M. Moqbul Hossain, learned Advocate appearing for petitioner candidly submits that finding of Courts below regarding non service of summons based on materials on record and Courts below concurrently held that summons were not properly served upon plaintiffs i.e. defendant nos.1 I and 14 of Title Suit no.04 of 1988. He lastly submits that there may be a direction to proceed with the suit. Mr. Jamaluddin Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for opposite party nos. 1-2 submits that he has no objection if Title Suit no.04 of 1988 be proceeded in accordance with law. 

10. In order to appreciate the submissions advanced by learned Counsels I have gone through revisional application, pleadings, all exhibits, other materials on record and given my anxious consideration to their submissions. 

11. Now the question calls for consideration whether Courts below committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing judgments and decrees. 

12. On going to the materials on record it transpires that plaintiffs instituted suit for setting aside exported judgment and decree dated 28.10.1991 passed in Title Suit no.04 of 1988 (exhbt.8). The plaintiffs claim that they were defendant nos.11 and 14 of Title Suit no.04 of 1988 but summons were not duly served upon them. The contesting defendants disowned such facts and claim that plaintiffs intentionally did not receive summons. 

13. It further transpires that Courts below concurrently held that summons were not duly served upon the plaintiffs. The learned Counsel for petitioner candidly submits that there is no misreading or non consideration of evidence on record regarding service of summons by Courts below. Having regard to facts I am of the view that summons upon defendant nos.11 and 14 of Title Suit no.04 of 1988 herein plaintiffs were not properly served. Therefore, I am in full agreement with views of Courts below. 

14. It is well settled that against ex-parte decree four kinds of relieves are available to an aggrieved party under the Code of Civil Procedure, those are: (1) Miscellaneous Case under IX Rule 13; (2) An appeal; (3) A Review under Order LXVII Rule 1; (4) A separate suit for setting aside the ex-parte decree. 

15. It has been decided in the case of Md. Wasiq Khan Vs. Md. Sabiq Khan and others 31 DLR (AD)51 that: when anybody suffers from an exported decree he can maintain a suit for setting aside the same. 

16. It is pertinent to mention that as exported judgment and decree passed in Title Suit no.04 of 1988 was set aside, so in my view, same should be proceeded with trial in accordance with law. In the case of Dharanidhar Aditya and others Hemanga Chandra Jana and others 21 CWN 1087, it has been held: "Decree setting aside ex-parte decree, effect of Court if bound to revive and proceed with trial of suit. Where an ex-parte decree is set aside by a Court of competent jurisdiction the effect is that the decree whereby the suit was terminated stands cancelled and the suit remains on the file of the Court as an undisposed of suit. In these circumstances it is incumbent upon the Court to proceed with the trial of the .suit and if the plaintiff does not wise to proceed with the trial of the suit, the Court must dismiss it but if the plaintiff desires to proceed with it, it must be tried in accordance with law. The fact that the suit terminated in an exported decree and not a consent decree, makes no difference in point of principle." This view receives support in the cases reported in 31. DLR (AD) 51 and 15 BLD-442. 

17. In the present case the suit was terminated in an ex-exported decree. That decree has been set aside by a Court of compete tent jurisdiction. The effect is that the decree whereby the suit was terminated stands cancelled and the suit remains on the file of the Court as an undisposed of suit. In these circumstances, it is incumbent upon the Court to proceed with the trial of the suit. If the plaintiffs do not wise to proceed with the trial of the suit the Court must dismiss it but if the plaintiffs desire to proceed with the suit it must be tried in accordance with law. 

18. In view of the discussions made above and the preponderant judicial views emerging out of the authorities referred to above, I am of the view that the trial of the suit will proceed in accordance with law. 

19. In the result, the Rule is disposed of without any order as to cost. The judgments and decrees of Courts below are hereby affirmed. The Title Suit no.04 of 1988 will stand revive and will be tried in accordance with law. Both parties are at liberty to adduce evidence in support of their respective claim and learned Judge of trial Court is directed to dispose of the suit on merit as early as possible. 

20. Office is directed to send down the records of this case at once with a copy of judgment for information and necessary action. 

End.
